text:
Patrick Kane turned 38 last week back where it all started. After stops in New York and Detroit, the first overall pick of 2007 is a Blackhawk again, wearing 88 and running the power play for a young team that just lost Connor Bedard to an injury reports call potentially lengthy. Kane has answered with a five-game point streak (a goal and seven assists) and has 17 points in 21 games, 9 of them on the power play.

He's still a passer first. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 95th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season, and his 15 assists fit. The goals are the oddity: 2 on 5.8 expected (the quality of his chances), a 4% shooting rate, and the kind of drought that usually ends for a player still getting looks. Five on five is the real worry, with Chicago taking 41% of the expected goals while he's out there. Our numbers project about 60 points, a fine season for a player who came in with 1,400 career points. Watch whether he can steer that power play without Bedard beside him.
headline: Patrick Kane, home again, is still setting the table
